title: Kubernetes operator reconciliation and durable transitions
purpose: Find reachable correctness failures in the Ledger Kubernetes control plane when reconciliation repeats, observations are stale, an external effect commits without a response, or the operator crashes and restarts between durable steps. Cover Cluster, Ledger, Credentials, Backup and BackupRun controllers and their deployed permissions and dependencies. Apply the companion evidence contract; exclude style, performance-only work, generic Kubernetes hardening, and guarantees not established by this repository.
invariants: Canonical StatefulSet metadata is trusted only when pod-config-hash is nonempty, the actual installed Pod-template ledger.formance.com/spec-hash is nonempty and metadata ledger.formance.com/pod-config-spec-hash equals that installed hash. Hash resolution and compatibility preservation must share this rule; marker presence, UID, generation or equal installed/desired hash strings cannot replace verified reconstruction. The association records the actual retained historical Pod hash when preserved. Normal/pre-scale writes stamp both metadata values atomically after final template resolution, before Raft effects; replacement snapshots stamp them after admission preview and before encoding/digesting, never by modifying an existing immutable journal. After completed recovery, a released Operator may preserve unknown metadata while changing the Pod hash: detect the broken pair, use exact reconstruction when possible, and add no storage-only rollout merely for association failure. In A-to-released-ServiceAccount-B-to-A, opaque equal templates without usable proof must report HashMigrationRequired; authentic B history must produce the A rollout. Valid-pair canonical precedence over leftover proof must still request later real nonstorage rollouts. Downgrade remains forbidden during active journal recovery; an old binary can itself roll its storage hash.

Failed attempted durable intent/journal preparation, including response loss, records a mutex-protected memory retry hold with one entry per Cluster namespace/name, retaining only its latest UID and full prepared payload digest: initially two seconds, exponential to 30 seconds. Compute the prepared payload as needed, then check the hold before Preparing condition or new intent CAS. The same hold must neither write intent/preparation conditions nor increment its attempt or slide its deadline under watch traffic. No durable attempt in that waiting pass plus direct APIReader proof of the same nonterminating Cluster UID and nil pointer permits independently safe mutable-workload/protection work with old templates; return a positive RequeueAfter, retaining an earlier positive requeue from normal work, and no preparation error unless another actual error occurs. Normal status may truthfully reflect availability. Record failed pointer CAS operations centrally once, including response loss; start records other post-intent failures, and failed Completed journal deletion also records. Scheduled waits record no failure. New UID/digest resets the hold; successful start or Completed-pointer clear removes matching state. Safe Preparing absence-abort retains the hold; NotFound/deletion removes the entry. Ten minutes without a failed attempt expires it after the retry deadline; there is no cardinality cap or active-entry eviction, and cleanup scans scale with recently failed Cluster count; restart resets this rate control, which is never security authority. Preserve failed-attempt continuation fences, journal trust and Preparing absence-abort with a requested two-second requeue; scheduling is advisory, not a guaranteed cadence.

For legacy migration without explicit proof, admission-normalize the desired Pod template with the installed hash through a dry-run Update of the existing StatefulSet before accepting exact released full-spec reconstruction. A difference requests the normal canonical-hash rollout even for a reconstructible hash, covering image/configuration/TLS changes and an implicit LEDGER_IMAGE_TAG change under existing RC/TLS/storage gates. Equal admitted templates preserve the installed hash automatically only after exact reconstruction. Dry-run errors publish ClaimTemplatesReady=False/AdmissionCheckFailed on the actual Cluster before canonical metadata or recovery intent/journal writes. This StatefulSet Update preview does not execute Pod Create admission or certify actual IAM/runtime access; the real Update still passes admission and rollout depends on the full Pod template revision. Only equal admitted templates without exact reconstruction leave external inputs ambiguous and require Cluster annotation ledger.formance.com/legacy-spec-hash-proof containing one JSON object with version 1, current StatefulSet sourceUID, installed Pod-template oldSpecHash and the fully effective historical ClusterSpec in spec. Verify exact version/UID/hash and recompute the released hash without current defaults. History includes the admitted spec after released applyDefaults, historical LEDGER_IMAGE_REPOSITORY/TAG values and omissions as hashed. Recompute canonical prior/current hashes: equality still requires admitted-template equality to preserve the installed Pod hash; nonstorage differences roll. Missing required proof reports HashMigrationRequired without advancing either workload hash or starting replacement. Malformed/foreign/stale/inconsistent explicit proof reports HashMigrationInvalid even if templates differ. Only a valid canonical/installed-hash association takes precedence over leftover proof and must not suppress later rollouts. Missing or broken association follows verified legacy migration without forcing a storage-only rollout. This metadata-only migration does not change the public CRD schema or authorize manual hash resets. Operational guidance must recommend upgrading the CRD and Operator with the declaration unchanged and waiting for a valid association before storage/ServiceAccount edits, not marker presence alone. If combined edits require history, only authentic prior declared inputs may be restored temporarily; independent PVC reconciliation and accepted live growth are not reversed. The ServiceAccount resource may already have been updated before a hash migration error; that error does not undo its write or refresh existing Pods. Keep strict historical proof as an alternative and require invalid supplied proof to be corrected or deliberately removed before the no-proof path.

The canonical Pod restart hash excludes WAL/data size, volumeAttributesClassName, storageClass and accessMode while retaining HostPath wiring and ServiceAccount configuration. Adding, replacing or removing ServiceAccount annotations still requests the normal Pod rollout, including with simultaneous storage edits: those annotations can affect Pod admission despite equal other template bytes. A differing trusted canonical StatefulSet metadata hash must not enter a generic admission-equality fallback. Verify actual rollout and effective runtime access separately from accepted template/hash writes.

After claim-template preparation fails, safe normal mutable-workload and volume-protection work with the old templates may continue only if no durable status-intent write was attempted, then the direct APIReader proves the same nonterminating Cluster UID has no recovery pointer. Mark the write phase immediately before the first actual intent Status.Patch and retain it through journal creation and typed errors with the original cause. Any error after that attempt blocks normal continuation, including rejection/no commit, response loss and a later NotFound. Retain the preparation condition/error and return it after permitted safe attempts. A pointer, uncertain read, stale cached absence or changed Cluster identity cannot authorize continuation; nil in-memory status is never sufficient. Standalone unbound ConfigMaps supply neither authority nor a block.

After StatefulSet recreation, a missing expected Pod reports ClaimTemplatesReady=False/AwaitingAdoption with its name and a short requeue while retaining the journal and pointer. Other Pod-read errors remain recovery failures. Completion still requires every expected Pod to exist, be nonterminating and be controlled by the exact replacement, in addition to the observed-generation and retained-storage identity guards.

Recovery Credentials projection reads current Credentials and their referenced Secrets directly from the API rather than relying on cached distribution observations. AuthKeysRolloutDeferred is removed only after the recovery pointer is nil and a normal StatefulSet reconciliation succeeds; that removal does not certify that every serving Pod has completed the resulting rollout. Legacy-hash dry-run errors must publish ClaimTemplatesReady=False/AdmissionCheckFailed on the actual Cluster even when reconciliation uses an effective TLS configuration copy.

Ledger spec.name and spec.clusterRef are fixed from CR creation by API-server CEL transition validation, including Pending or ambiguous creation outcomes and edits combined with promotion or index changes. Rejected edits must leave the stored cleanup target unchanged. Installing the rules does not recover pre-existing drift; follow the documented stopped-operator inventory/recovery procedure before installation. This boundary does not prove external ledger ownership or fence a Cluster recreated under the same name, and does not strengthen best-effort deletion into guaranteed cleanup.

Repeated reconciliation of the same logical resource must converge under the documented API semantics without duplicating irreversible effects or undoing completed work. Establish logical identity from namespace, name, UID, generation, external operation identity and ownership as applicable; a name reused by a replacement CR is not proof of continuity with the old CR.

Every reported defect must start from an admitted CR or another reachable deployment state and follow the real manager registration, watch/predicate or requeue path, permissions, controller guards and external call to the violated postcondition. A fake-client state forbidden by CRD validation, absent production dependency, or unsupported configuration alone is not evidence of reachability.

Resource creation, adoption, update and deletion must respect controller ownership, namespace and UID boundaries, selectors and retention semantics. Deletion must not recreate resources for a terminating owner or mutate resources belonging to another owner. Finalizers, where used for external cleanup, must survive retries until cleanup is established; garbage collection without a finalizer is valid where it satisfies the declared lifecycle contract.

Status and conditions must describe the observed resource and generation according to their documented meaning. EventSink Delivering is False for a runtime startup or delivery error, Unknown when the cursor is zero without error, and True after nonzero cursor progress without error. Filtered or internal logs can advance the cursor without Publish, so True alone does not certify external delivery. A persisted Ready, Succeeded, applied hash or terminal phase must not falsely certify an unfinished effect or suppress required recovery. Failed status persistence and stale reads must have a reachable convergence path when status is needed for correctness; ordinary temporary observation lag is not itself a defect.

A Kubernetes API write, pod exec, ledgerctl call or backup Job can commit its effect before timing out, losing its response, or failing to persist controller status. Such an error is an unknown outcome rather than proof of no effect. Retry or compensation must establish identity and authoritative postconditions before repeating a non-idempotent effect; do not invent exactly-once guarantees where no contract supplies them.

Backup scheduling, manual BackupRun execution, Job association, result extraction and parent summary updates must preserve the identity and outcome of each execution across conflicts, duplicate events and operator restarts. Success requires the corresponding completed backup result. Run history garbage collection must preserve the documented Kubernetes-history boundary and must not be treated as S3 backup-object retention.

Restore deployment must preserve the intended cluster identity, mode, storage and supplied credentials across reconciles and restarts. Trace the actual handoff between spec.restore, the restore-mode process, external download/finalize commands and the return to normal mode; ordinary readiness or a pod restart must not be taken as proof of completed restore. This is orchestration correctness, not a claim that a Restore controller or automatic restore transaction exists.

Scale-down must establish the required Raft membership removal postcondition before reducing the relevant replicas and disposing of their volumes. Before Raft exec, the preparatory StatefulSet write resolves the workload hash and commits both canonical pod-config-hash and pod-config-spec-hash association metadata atomically after final prepared Pod-template resolution while retaining the previous replica count. The association records the actual installed hash, including a preserved historical hash. An API write failure prevents Raft work; an exec failure after commit retains the valid pair so the next pass retries Raft instead of invalidating the original historical proof against the controller's changed Pod hash. The marker alone proves neither rollout nor membership completion. An already-absent member and a removal committed before an opaque exec failure must be handled using authoritative membership evidence. Reconciliation after partial removal, changed desired replicas or operator restart must preserve the intended member/node identity and must not destroy still-required storage or bypass documented quorum and force-removal preconditions.

TLS mode transitions, certificate and CA references, cluster secrets and Credentials reconciliation must preserve intended peer connectivity and authorization across rolling updates, rotation, deletion and operator restart. Distinguish desired template state from the mode and keys actually loaded by running pods; an intermediate optional TLS mode is permitted only within the documented transition. Reject unsupported or missing inputs according to established contracts without silently weakening trust or losing ownership of secrets. Removing spec.tls or clearing its certificate reference while disabling TLS must retain the prior certificate and CA references through optional mode. Persist rollout recovery state before StatefulSet mutation or orphan deletion, retain it until disabled rollout convergence, and reconstruct an absent StatefulSet from that state after restart. The certificate Secret stays externally owned and must remain available until disable completes. New backup Job transport and certificate/CA configuration must come from one current StatefulSet template controlled by the Cluster; a missing workload must retry provisioning without plaintext fallback and a foreign owner must be rejected. Existing Jobs retain their persisted configuration. In-pod Ledger and EventSink ledgerctl callers must return a retryable lookup error before exec while the StatefulSet is absent and read its current mode after recreation.

Changes to WAL/data PVC size, VolumeClaimTemplates, storage layout and deletion-protection labels must preserve data and resource ownership through the actual supported transition, including orphan/recreate/adopt. Distinguish template request, existing PVC request, bound capacity and mounted filesystem capacity. Do not infer unconditional live expansion or shrink support from a size field, or bypass StorageClass, CSI, admission-policy and retention prerequisites.

For PVC-backed WAL/data, the configured size is a minimum on existing claims even when autoExpansion is absent or disabled. Reconciliation may raise requests but must not shrink or replace claims, discard larger auto-grown capacity, or change volume identity. Existing claim-template minima are nondecreasing: use the greater of the prior template minimum and configured size, without copying automatic live-PVC growth into templates or the Cluster spec. A lower configured size must not cause perpetual recreation. autoExpansion.maximumSize limits automatic decisions only, not explicit GitOps size requests.

A nonempty WAL/data volumeAttributesClassName requests in-place modification of existing PVCs through Kubernetes/CSI, with compatible API, driver and sidecar prerequisites. Report unsupported clearing, API rejection, pending CSI work and observed CSI failure without silently clearing the class or certifying a requested profile as applied. Existing storageClass/accessMode migrations remain unsupported, and this feature does not change hostPath paths/layout or authorize direct AWS/PV-capacity changes. WALStorageReady/DataStorageReady describe existing claim convergence; ClaimTemplatesReady describes template recovery and must not certify mounted capacity or effective profile by itself.

StorageClass/accessMode declaration differences must not block size/profile claim-template alignment: copy the existing template class/access modes unchanged. Explicitly selecting the effective default class of existing PVCs is accepted even when the template omitted the class; both PVC reconciliation and template size/profile progress must remain possible without migration. Live PVC validation separately reports genuine migration as StorageUnsupported without changing class/access modes. Preserve mutable workload progress, independently safe owned-PVC growth, ownership, identity and no-shrink guards. Unsupported VAC clearing and incompatible claim layouts retain separate failure contracts.

Before orphan-deleting a StatefulSet for a WAL/data size/profile claim-template update, prepare independent source/replacement copies and retained identities under the existing source/Pod/binding/admission guards, encode the full payload once, and CAS nil status.claimTemplateRecovery to a protected Preparing intent with sourceUID, full payloadSHA256 and digest-derived configMapName before ConfigMap creation. Require the same nonterminating Cluster UID and prepared generation, no other operation, and API preservation of the whole intent. Create exact immutable bytes; AlreadyExists reuse requires fresh preparation, durable matching intent and direct owner/nontermination/immutability/full-digest verification, never overwrite. After direct full journal authentication, decode only authenticated bytes and validate journal version, sourceUID and workload/claim structure before UID binding. Bind configMapUID by expected-Preparing CAS and verify persistence, then directly reread and reauthenticate the journal against that bound UID before dependencies, deletion or creation; missing or changed journals stop the pass. Preserve the prior complete Pod template, replica count and selector. Reconstruct interrupted prefixes before later spec validation or workload mutations. After orphan deletion can have occurred, retain recovery until the exact owned nonterminating replacement matches saved spec/operation identity, observedGeneration is at least generation, all expected nonterminating Pods are adopted and retained PVC/PV UIDs and claimRef bindings are verified. Ready/Updated replicas are not completion requirements; source rollout readiness remains required before deletion. A same-UID nonterminating original source whose generation/readiness changed can complete and clean the obsolete plan for normal repair; absent, terminating or replacement sources cannot. All pointer transitions compare the whole expected previous pointer plus optimistic resourceVersion and never overwrite a newer operation. Mark Completed before journal deletion, then clear only that expected pointer.

Protected Cluster status authorizes journal bytes; ConfigMap ownerReference, structure, name or a digest supplied only by that ConfigMap does not. SHA256 is domain-separated over Cluster UID, namespace, fixed journal base and exact once-encoded complete JSON; the name appends the first 32 hex characters while status retains the full lowercase digest. Every active resume verifies active status, journal name/UID/owner, nontermination, immutability and full digest before decoding or deriving dependencies; decoded sourceUID must match status. Nil status never adopts a standalone journal and its presence alone must not block normal work. Same-payload reuse still requires fresh full preparation and durable matching intent; different payloads derive different names. Unbound late ConfigMaps may remain for Cluster GC, without workload authority. Required source/digest/name fields fail closed without retroactive authentication migration because this feature is unpublished; no journal, Ledger data, Raft, audit or protocol version changes.

Preparing has empty configMapUID and completed=false. Direct named-journal NotFound permits expected-pointer CAS clear only after direct reads establish the same nonterminating Cluster UID, a valid Preparing pointer and the expected Cluster-controlled nonterminating StatefulSet with saved sourceUID. Readiness, source generation and latest CR validity are irrelevant; no dependencies or old claims are read, no workload or journal is mutated, and success returns handled plus a two-second requeue without normal writes in that pass. Missing/deleting/replaced/foreign sources and uncertain reads fail closed. Bind and abort compare the same Preparing pointer so only one wins; a late journal after abort remains unbound.

Active requires bound configMapUID and a missing active journal is a hard failure. Completed also requires a bound UID, but cleanup checks journal owner/UID and deletes with UID/resourceVersion preconditions without reading payload, requiring immutability or reconciling dependencies. Payload corruption must not strand completed cleanup; foreign UID still fails. A lost delete response can resume from NotFound, then clear only the exact expected Completed pointer.

During active size/profile recovery, reconcile independent dependencies from the trusted saved StatefulSet wiring and geometry without changing its Pod template. When the snapshot mounts auth keys, current Credentials projection must not delete that ConfigMap; no matches produce an explicit empty key set and unresolved matching keys retain fail-safe handling. Retain live spec.additionalLabels on independent auth-key ConfigMap and cluster-secret writes. Maintain the existing cluster-secret token only when required by the saved workload and apply the current protection toggle to saved replicas/claim names. Recovery protection must verify journal PVC/PV UIDs and binding and fence patches with UID/resourceVersion preconditions; predictable names alone must never authorize mutation of replaced or rebound storage. Newer invalid auth/TLS/replica fields must not select dependency inputs. Dependency errors must be reported without preventing the recovery attempt. Services, NetworkPolicy and other normal resources remain deferred. AuthKeysRolloutDeferred=True/StorageRecovery reports that Ed25519 keys and authorization metadata are loaded once at boot: ConfigMap convergence is not runtime revocation, scope reduction or rotation. The startup loader rejects an empty key set, so explicit removal can prevent restarted Pods with saved key-file wiring from starting; it does not disable authentication. The required normal rollout waits for recovery/cleanup, but an adopted unready/OOM/empty-key restarted Pod must not prevent cleanup and a return to normal workload repair. Missing/unadopted Pods, unobserved generation or identity failures still block recovery. Verify the eventual rollout and runtime authorization separately; do not invent an automatic emergency override.

Normalize the desired Pod template through admission dry-run Update of a copy of the existing StatefulSet before comparing equality with the live template; API defaults, including probe timeout/success threshold, must not falsely block recovery as WaitingForRollout. Desired-template normalization, replacement creation and legacy-hash dry-runs require available dry-run-capable webhooks. Normalization/legacy-hash failures publish ClaimTemplatesReady=False/AdmissionCheckFailed on the actual Cluster. Admission must preserve replacement settings; rejection, timeout or mutation must not fall back to skipping validation or rolling Pods for a storage-only edit. A replacement differing from the committed spec/operation identity remains RecoveryFailed. Preserve journals, claims and identities while correcting admission or restoring the exact trusted snapshot where Kubernetes permits it. StatefulSet absence can produce Pending/Ready=False/0-N despite surviving Pods, and Cluster deletion during the orphan window does not establish complete orphan-Pod cleanup.

Finish a current workload rollout using existing claim templates and Pod storage wiring before size/profile template recreation; a combined scale-up may wait for the new claim settings. During active snapshot recovery, freeze later scale, image and TLS mutations until the exact saved replacement has its generation observed, all expected nonterminating Pods adopted and retained storage identities verified, without requiring ReadyReplicas or UpdatedReplicas, then clean up recovery state before applying later desired changes. PVC patches and CSI effects are independently durable; a spec revert cannot undo accepted growth or imply cancellation of a profile change. Profile rollback requires another supported nonempty class, and recovery must not depend on manually deleting the snapshot. Do not generalize this size/profile recovery contract to historical hostPath/PVC layout transitions. Recognize released full-spec hashes and preserve the PodTemplate hash for storage-only changes across recreation and subsequent reconciliation; real workload changes still roll out.

For an RC target, establish the running source RC and require its immediate successor on the same release line and a converged prior rollout before changing the StatefulSet. During an adjacent RC upgrade that also changes immutable VolumeClaimTemplates, first roll the new image with the existing WAL/data Pod storage wiring and claim templates; recreate the StatefulSet for the requested storage only after that image rollout converges. An absent StatefulSet with retained Pods or PVCs must not silently bypass source verification after an interrupted recreation.

After each externally durable step, a fresh operator process with no previous in-memory reconcile state must be able to observe enough evidence to resume, safely compensate, or report an explicit actionable failure under the documented contract. Include crash windows between effects, owner/finalizer writes, status writes and cleanup, plus leader-election handoff. Do not assume an atomic transaction across Kubernetes, Ledger and object storage.

Rollback of a desired-spec change and compensation after partial failure must account for already committed effects. Reverting a CR, cancelling a request, or restoring an in-memory object is not rollback of Raft membership, a backup, a secret write or a PVC deletion. Supported recovery must not resurrect obsolete work or erase unrelated/newer effects; upgrades from v3.0.0-rc.1 onward must preserve data, while arbitrary binary downgrade is outside scope.

Preparation owns PreparationFailed only before its initial handoff to recovery resume. After handoff, orphan-delete and replacement-create errors must retain the resume RecoveryFailed condition, bound journal/pointer and original error through the durable-write continuation fence, with single failure accounting. A fresh reconciler must retry the same operation safely. The recovery error handler must also cover the initial uncached Cluster refresh and its identity checks before journal authentication or binding; these failures cannot retain Recreating. RecoveryFailed requires a known recovery pointer, including Preparing after handoff or one discovered by a successful direct refresh. An ordinary nil-pointer probe must propagate an initial refresh error without creating or relabeling ClaimTemplatesReady.
adversarial_questions: Can stale canonical A metadata survive a released Operator installing ServiceAccount B/full Pod hash B, then suppress the required rollout back to desired A? Do both resolution and preservation reject absent/empty/broken associations, use exact legacy reconstruction without an extra storage rollout, require strict history for opaque equal templates, and roll to A with authentic B proof? Are actual retained historical hashes associated after final template resolution at normal/pre-scale writes and before replacement snapshot encoding, without UID/generation binding or immutable-journal edits?

Can rejected or response-lost intent/journal writes plus Preparing clear/watch events bypass the retry hold and create another intent immediately? Does each namespace/name/UID/full-digest hold retain its deadline/attempt during watches, avoid intent/preparation-condition churn and permit safe normal work only with no durable attempt and the direct nil-pointer identity fence? Do successful start/Completed clear, Preparing-abort retention, new UID/digest, restart, deletion and ten-minute stale expiry with one entry per namespace/name behave as rate control without authorizing recovery or hiding availability failures?

For every unpaired released hash without proof, including an exactly reconstructible hash, does StatefulSet Update dry-run admission precede preservation? Does a differing admitted desired template request the normal canonical-hash image/configuration/TLS rollout, including a changed implicit LEDGER_IMAGE_TAG, while equal templates preserve the installed hash only after exact reconstruction and otherwise require history for ambiguous external inputs? Do preview errors publish AdmissionCheckFailed on the actual Cluster before canonical metadata or recovery intent/journal writes, including through the real caller with an effective TLS copy? Is preview evidence limited to StatefulSet Update admission rather than Pod Create admission or actual IAM/runtime access? Can template equality, a supplied canonical assertion, current ServiceAccount values or current defaults substitute for that history? Does legacy-spec-hash-proof bind exact version/source UID/installed hash and reproduce the released hash from admitted historical spec, released applyDefaults, historical image environment and omissions before canonical comparison? Does invalid explicit proof remain invalid even with differing templates, missing required proof leave both hashes unchanged, exact reconstruction remain automatic and leftover proof become harmless only with a valid canonical/installed-hash association?

Can the preparatory scale-down write advance the Pod-template hash without atomically recording both canonical and installed-hash association metadata after final template resolution, then reject its own valid historical proof after a Raft exec failure? Does a failed API write prevent Raft calls, and does a committed preparation plus failed exec allow a fresh reconciler to retry membership removal before reducing replicas while preserving storage?

Can storage-hash migration or admitted-template equality hide an addition, replacement or removal of ServiceAccount annotations that should recreate Pods for admission inputs? Do modern canonical sources roll on nonstorage changes while size/profile/class/access-mode declaration edits alone retain the installed Pod hash, and do HostPath wiring changes remain visible?

Can a preparation error before the first durable intent-write attempt skip safe mutable-workload/protection progress despite a direct same-UID nonterminating Cluster with nil pointer, or can any error after that attempted status write incorrectly permit it? Include rejected/no-commit and lost responses before CMCreate, preserve phase/original cause through typed errors, and ignore standalone ConfigMaps when no protected operation exists. Can stale cached absence, uncertain direct reads or changed Cluster identity bypass the fence?

Does a missing expected Pod after recreation remain AwaitingAdoption with a named ordinal and short retry, rather than become a raw NotFound failure or permit early cleanup? After that ordinal is restored, do exact ownership, nontermination, generation and storage guards still apply? Are other API read errors preserved as recovery failures?

Can stale cached Credentials or Secret reads retain removed authorization during recovery? Does AuthKeysRolloutDeferred remain until recovery cleanup and a successful normal StatefulSet pass, without misrepresenting its removal as runtime rollout completion? Are legacy-hash preview errors persisted on the actual Cluster rather than only a temporary effective TLS copy?

Can a defaulted effective PVC class made explicit in the CR, genuine class migration or access-mode drift block size/profile template alignment despite copying the existing class/modes unchanged? Distinguish live StorageUnsupported migration diagnostics from supported size/profile progress and unsupported VAC clearing/layout errors. Prove mutable workload progress, independently safe growth and unchanged class/access-mode fields and identities.

After a rejected or lost delete response, can the original same-UID nonterminating StatefulSet become unready without a generation change and prevent a later workload repair forever? Is stale-plan completion/cleanup durable and restricted to the original source before deletion, including absent, terminating and replacement-UID counterexamples?

During active recovery, do current Credentials changes reach the retained mounted ConfigMap, including no matches and unresolved matching keys? Do independent ConfigMap/cluster-secret writes retain live additionalLabels and the existing token while saved wiring/geometry stays authoritative despite invalid later spec edits? Can replaced PVC/PV UIDs or a rebind redirect protection writes? Can dependency errors block restoration? Does an adopted but unready/OOM/empty-key restarted Pod incorrectly keep the journal and normal repair/auth rollout frozen? Which serving Pods actually loaded the new keys, and which missing/adoption/generation/identity failures still require recovery?

Do dry-run webhook failures or admission mutations stay visible without an unsafe rollout fallback? For a mismatched replacement, does guidance preserve committed journals and storage identities? Can aggregate workload absence be mistaken for actual Pod loss, or Cluster deletion during the orphan window be mistaken for guaranteed Pod cleanup?

Can a Ledger target edit reach creation, promotion, index reconciliation or deletion before rejection? Check separate name/cluster changes, combined mutable-field changes, Pending and deletion-pending resources through real admission. For old stored drift, can installing immutability freeze the wrong target or prevent correction, and is pre-install recovery explicit?

Which reconcilers are registered by the actual manager, with which clients, watches, predicates, namespace restrictions, RBAC and leader-election configuration? Can a dependency change or recovered transient failure trigger another pass without unrelated resource churn?

For each multi-step reconcile, what is changed only in memory, what is committed to the API server, what commits in Ledger or S3, and what residual state remains after every prefix? Which fresh-process observation drives the next action?

Can AlreadyExists, NotFound, a resourceVersion conflict or a lost response refer to a same-name replacement object? Before adopting, mutating, execing into or deleting it, which UID, owner, selector and cluster checks establish the intended target?

What happens when deletion starts between finalizer registration, external ledger/index/credential creation, cleanup and finalizer removal? Are GC and retention policies actually active in the deployed chart, and do they cover cross-scope resources?

Can a status write fail after a successful effect, or a terminal status be persisted before result capture? Does the next pass recover from observed external state, repeat the effect, or skip unfinished work? Is the alleged status failure material to a consumer or convergence?

Can a scheduled run be duplicated or lost between BackupRun creation and parent schedule advancement? What happens when a parent changes, a Job or result pod disappears, multiple Job attempts exist, or a completed run is pruned before the parent observes its result?

Does backup result extraction bind the payload to the right run/Job/pod attempt and type? How are malformed, absent, truncated or stale termination messages and CLI output distinguished from successful backup completion?

During restore, which actor changes mode, downloads, validates and finalizes? What happens if the operator or pod restarts before or after each handoff, or the CR returns to normal mode prematurely? Which readiness signal represents serving state versus management availability?

If one scale-down removal commits and exec returns an opaque error, membership observation is stale or fails, a later removal fails, or the StatefulSet update succeeds before PVC cleanup fails, what happens on retry and after restart? Can a scale-up reversal reuse an old ordinal/PVC or a tombstoned node identity?

When image/config changes coincide with scale-down or TLS migration, which live pod mode, endpoint, CA and token does ledgerctl use? Are intermediate TLS phases reconstructed from actual rollout state after operator restart or a desired-mode reversal?

Do referenced certificate, CA, token and credential changes reach all relevant consumers? Can deletion, failed regeneration, stale caches or a same-name Secret replacement leave an accepted credential active incorrectly, discard a valid key, or point a workload at another owner's secret?

For a PVC growth request, what actually updates the old claims and what only changes templates for future claims? Can orphan deletion succeed before its response is lost, or the operator restart before replacement/adoption, and leave pods, claims, labels or retained data stranded? Is unsupported growth rejected or merely ambiguous in the API contract?

With template 100Gi, an auto-grown PVC request/capacity of 200Gi and configured size 150Gi, does reconciliation preserve that PVC while installing only a 150Gi template minimum? After a configured decrease, repeated reconciles and scale-out, do templates remain nondecreasing without a perpetual recreate loop? Can an explicit minimum above autoExpansion.maximumSize be blocked by the unrelated automatic cap or cooldown, or can automatic growth rewrite the CR/template?

Does a nonempty profile edit reach every existing WAL/data claim without replacing its UID or binding? Which supported Kubernetes/CSI observations distinguish requested, pending, failed and applied profiles? Can unsupported clearing, missing classes, driver mismatch, storageClass/accessMode edits or stale status produce silent drift or false storage readiness? Do concurrent storage/template condition writers preserve each other's conditions?

At every snapshot-create, orphan-delete, replacement-create, adoption and snapshot-cleanup boundary, what remains durable after error, response loss or process replacement? Can foreign/corrupt journals, same-name resources, changed selectors or stale reads redirect recovery or erase its saved intent? Before cleanup, are exact saved replacement spec/operation identity, ownership, observed generation, all expected nonterminating Pods adopted and retained PVC/PV identities verified? Can zero Ready/Updated replicas incorrectly prevent completion, or an unobserved generation/missing/unadopted Pod incorrectly pass? Does cleanup avoid another recreation and permit later normal repair without certifying runtime availability?

Can ConfigMap ownerReference/structure, self-declared digest or a same-name source authorize journal consumption without a preceding protected status intent? Are exact once-encoded bytes, domain-separated full digest, sourceUID, digest-derived name, immutable journal and bound UID checked before every active decode/dependency/workload path? Can AlreadyExists overwrite bytes, an old CRD prune intent fields, or a status retry replace a newer whole pointer?

For Preparing with a directly absent journal, can abort clear a different/newer operation, require readiness/generation/current-spec validity unnecessarily, or read dependencies/old claims before the same-UID controlled nonterminating source is proven? Does successful abort stop and requeue? If bind races abort, can both win, and can a late unbound ConfigMap block normal work or acquire authority without fresh preparation and durable intent? Can corrupt completed payload prevent UID/owner/RV-fenced cleanup?

Does saved size/profile recovery run before current-spec validation and scale/image/TLS mutations after a restart, including when no StatefulSet exists or the CR is edited mid-recovery? Does a combined workload/storage edit first converge the workload with old storage wiring, then recreate with the prior complete Pod template, replica count and selector? Can reverting Git undo or hide only some already-accepted PVC/CSI effects?

Can a skipped RC, an unconverged source rollout, or an absent StatefulSet with retained Pods/PVCs pass the predecessor gate? When an RC image update coincides with hostPath/PVC or claim-template changes, does the interim Pod template still reference only the existing storage sources and mounts until recreation?

Which retry/backoff and event sources recover after API-server, exec, cert-manager, CSI or object-store availability returns? A transient outage is expected; what concrete mechanism makes the failure permanent, destructive or falsely successful after recovery?

Which tests cross the real production guards and assert final resource UIDs, membership, data, credentials and phase, and which only compare desired manifests or reconstruct an impossible fake state? Can a test pass by reading through another healthy pod while the intended PVC or restored node is wrong?

For backup S3 Secret references, do Jobs preserve same-namespace, non-optional key references across reconciliation and fresh runs? Distinguish a Running BackupRun awaiting a missing Secret/key from a successful backup; Secret changes affect newly started containers and must not be described as live environment updates. Confidentiality of resource serialization belongs to sensitive-data-exposure-boundaries.

When spec.tls is removed or enabled=false clears secretName, where are the previous certificate and CA references retained? Does a failed recovery-status write prevent StatefulSet mutation/deletion? After orphan deletion and controller replacement, can an absent StatefulSet incorrectly bootstrap plaintext while TLS-only pods remain? Distinguish disabled template selection from observed rollout convergence and retained-state cleanup.

Can a new backup Job combine optional/required workload mode with absent desired spec.tls and lose its CA or certificate mount? Are mode and trust resolved from one owned StatefulSet snapshot? Does absent workload cause retry, and can a foreign-owner resource be accepted? Which configuration remains authoritative once the Job is persisted? Do both in-pod ledgerctl callers reject a missing StatefulSet before exec rather than selecting plaintext?

Does the normal manager initiation guard compare an admission-normalized desired Pod template with the existing template? Can defaulted probes produce permanent WaitingForRollout despite a settled source? Do rejected or timed-out normalization updates remain visible as AdmissionCheckFailed without orphan deletion or an unsafe fallback?
dynamic_checks_to_consider: Test valid canonical/installed-hash associations, missing/empty/broken pairs, historical retained Pod hashes, valid-pair precedence over leftover proof and both shared trust call sites. Drive A-to-released-ServiceAccount-B-to-A through unit and API/normal-manager paths: no usable proof plus opaque equal templates must report HashMigrationRequired without certifying B as A; authentic B proof must request actual A rollout and publish a valid pair. A broken pair alone must preserve the installed Pod hash when exact reconstruction succeeds and StatefulSet Update dry-run admits an equal template. Assert atomic pair/template writes at normal and preparatory pre-Raft updates and pair persistence in the replacement snapshot before encoding/digesting; do not mutate journals to retrofit it. Preserve genuine released RC/TLS fixtures by removing both modern annotations, retaining all original regression triggers. Accepted writes do not prove actual Pod admission or IAM access.

Use deterministic time to verify two-second initial/exponential/30-second-capped retry holds per namespace/name/UID/full digest, unchanged deadline and attempt during repeated waits, successful-start/Completed-clear matching resets, Preparing-abort retention, new UID/digest resets, deletion/NotFound cleanup, one entry per namespace/name, ten-minute expiry after the deadline without active-entry eviction, and concurrent access. In a bounded normal-manager envtest, verify real ResourceQuota admission denial with explicitly published quota usage and count Cluster events/status changes and real intent/clear transitions over watches; require bounded retry writes, no orphan delete while denied, and progress after removing denial. Include durable intent/journal response loss and safe mutable repair during a hold only through the direct same-UID/nonterminating/nil-pointer fence with no durable attempt in that pass. Assert positive RequeueAfter retaining any earlier positive normal-work requeue, with nil preparation error unless another actual error occurs. Unit tests separately assert unchanged waiting conditions and fenced protection work. Concurrent status writers can race PreparationFailed sampling, so the manager test uses actual intent/abort transitions and never promises a stable diagnostic sample. After quota removal, verify authenticated/bound journal, real orphan-delete request, replacement with the requested template and Completed cleanup with stable PVC/PV identities. Explicitly simulate GC/adoption/observed generation and restore the one-Pod fixture after mutable scale-up; do not claim actual GC, StatefulSet-controller, CSI or Raft evidence. Distinguish retry churn from legitimate normal availability status writes; do not run denial/load scenarios on a user cluster.

Journal-absence assertions must check nil protected status plus the actual prefix-filtered ConfigMap list or recorded ConfigMap Create attempts, never a vacant historical fixed name. Cleanup must use the captured real digest-derived key. Preserve every preflight, destructive-boundary, source UID, digest and PVC/PV assertion while updating these oracles.

Use genuine released sources without either modern hash annotation or proof, including the original RC/TLS regression triggers and hashes of historical effective specs. For an unrecognized hash and equal admitted templates, assert HashMigrationRequired and unchanged Pod/canonical hashes and workload identity. With a differing admitted template, assert the normal canonical-hash image/configuration/TLS rollout: cover adjacent RC tags both explicit and omitted with changed LEDGER_IMAGE_TAG, preserve RC/TLS gates and wait for workload convergence before storage recreation. Supply version-1 legacy-spec-hash-proof bound to current UID/installed hash using trusted admitted history after released applyDefaults, historical LEDGER_IMAGE_REPOSITORY/TAG and original omissions: recompute the released hash, preserve storage-only installed Pod hashes only after canonical and admitted-template equality, and roll on historical/current ServiceAccount differences. Reject malformed/trailing/unknown JSON fields, wrong version, absent spec, stale/foreign UID/hash and inconsistent historical values as HashMigrationInvalid even when templates differ. For a recognized exactly reconstructible released hash without proof, exercise equal, differing and failed StatefulSet Update previews: equality preserves the installed hash and records the valid canonical association, a difference returns the desired canonical-hash template, and failure publishes AdmissionCheckFailed on the actual Cluster with unchanged StatefulSet template/hash metadata and no recovery pointer/journal writes or orphan deletion. Cover the real StatefulSet reconciliation caller, including an effective TLS copy, rather than certifying that mutation/status boundary only at the resolver. Restore admission and prove a real retry succeeds. Retain invalid explicit proof rejection with both equal and differing templates. StatefulSet Update previews do not execute Pod Create admission or prove actual IAM/runtime access. After canonical migration, remove proof and also retain stale proof through a later real ServiceAccount edit/replacement; assert a valid canonical/installed-hash association wins. Cover unit and real API/normal-manager paths; do not replace genuine released triggers with synthetic canonical metadata or claim mixed-version communication/runtime access from requested writes.

Combine a genuine released hash, valid proof, ServiceAccount change and scale-down. Assert the preparatory StatefulSet update retains the old replicas and commits the prepared Pod template plus canonical pod-config-hash and pod-config-spec-hash metadata in the same write after final template resolution and before Raft exec. Assert the association equals the actual retained Pod hash, including historical hashes. Reject that write and assert no Raft call. Separately commit it, fail the first exec, then retry with a fresh reconciler: retain the durable template/valid pair, assert the original proof is not rejected as stale, actually attempt Raft again and verify final replicas only after the membership postcondition. Preserve claim identities; marker-only assertions do not prove rollout or Raft completion.

Across modern canonical and released full-spec sources, add, replace and remove ServiceAccount annotations with and without simultaneous size/profile edits. Through focused unit and normal manager paths, assert the requested ServiceAccount and new Pod-template hash, with old claims retained until workload rollout converges. Separately vary only class/access-mode declarations and assert no Pod rollout while supported storage progress and unsupported migration diagnostics remain intact. Hash/template assertions establish the requested rollout; actual admission injection and runtime access require a serving-workload fixture.

Fail preparation before the first durable status-intent attempt and prove a direct same-UID nonterminating Cluster with nil pointer; assert safe mutable-workload/protection progress with old templates and returned preparation error, even with a standalone unbound ConfigMap. Restore the prerequisite and prove retry. Separately reject/no-commit or lose the response to the first status-intent write, then return NotFound for a journal; assert zero normal mutable-workload continuation. Include journal-create/bind response loss, delayed/unknown writes, stale cached nil pointer, failed direct reads and Cluster replacement/deletion. Preserve typed attempted-write phase and original errors through joins.

After recreation, omit one expected ordinal while preserving an exact owned replacement and retained storage. Assert AwaitingAdoption names that Pod, returns the recovery requeue interval, and keeps both journal and pointer incomplete. Restore the Pod, verify nontermination/exact replacement ownership and complete guarded cleanup. Keep other Pod-read errors, terminating/unadopted Pods, unobserved generation and changed bindings as independent negative controls; envtest fixture ownership updates do not establish actual controller adoption.

Give the cached client stale Credentials/Secret distribution observations while the direct API contains removal or rotation; assert recovery projection follows the live API. Verify AuthKeysRolloutDeferred survives an active pointer, pending auth or failed normal StatefulSet pass, and clears after pointer cleanup plus a successful normal pass without claiming runtime rollout completion. Reject a legacy-hash dry-run while effective TLS configuration differs from the desired Cluster and assert ClaimTemplatesReady=False/AdmissionCheckFailed persists on the actual CR.

From a source template with an omitted class and PVCs defaulted to gp3, explicitly select gp3, change a Pod annotation/image and request size/profile growth with automatic expansion disabled and enabled. Assert mutable workload progress, safe owned-PVC growth, template size/profile alignment, unchanged template/PVC class/access modes and stable UIDs/bindings; do not expect UnsupportedChange for the declaration mismatch. Separately request a genuinely different class/access mode: assert StorageUnsupported without field migration while supported template alignment, normal workload progress and independently safe growth continue. Keep unsupported VAC clearing and layout cases separate.

Reject an orphan delete once, leave the same original UID nonterminating, then make its rollout unready without changing generation. Reconcile with a fresh controller, persist obsolete-plan completion, clean up the journal, and apply a real image/configuration repair before replanning and completing recovery. Assert attempt count and final resource identity; separately prove no cancellation when deletion has started, the source is absent or a replacement UID exists.

With a trusted active journal and frozen Pod template, remove all matching Credentials, narrow scopes, rotate resolved keys and leave another matched key unresolved. Assert explicit empty projection on no matches, no mounted ConfigMap deletion, fail-safe unresolved-key handling, retained cluster-secret token and protection based on saved claim names/replicas with the current toggle. Change later auth/TLS/replica fields to invalid values and inject dependency errors; assert restoration still runs from the snapshot and errors remain visible. Assert AuthKeysRolloutDeferred=True/StorageRecovery and distinguish empty-set startup rejection from auth disablement. In a real serving workload, prove old running Pods retain boot-loaded authorization until the subsequent normal rollout, then verify new authorization per Pod; projection-only tests cannot prove revocation. Change live additionalLabels during recovery and assert those labels remain on independently reconciled auth-key ConfigMaps and cluster Secrets without changing the saved Pod template or existing token.

Reject or time out desired-template normalization/replacement/legacy-hash dry-runs and mutate admission output, then restore the prerequisite and retry without a fallback rollout. Introduce a replacement spec/operation-identity mismatch and assert RecoveryFailed with journal/claims preserved; correct admission or the permitted live spec exactly and verify convergence. With real Kubernetes controllers, inspect surviving Pods and identities during StatefulSet absence and intentional Cluster deletion; separate aggregate Ready status from serving state and actual orphan cleanup. Envtest alone does not prove GC, adoption or CSI behavior.

Use the real API server and generated base/Helm CRDs to accept Ledger creates, no-op updates, index edits and same-target mirror promotion while rejecting name and clusterRef edits. With two distinguishable ledgers and two healthy Clusters, assert rejected updates preserve the stored target, then delete the CR and verify only its original ledger is deleted while unrelated sentinel data remains. Include Pending and deletion-pending updates; do not substitute fake-client behavior for CEL admission evidence.

Inspect existing operator unit/envtest/Chainsaw cases and their module, API schema, fake-client limitations and assertions first. The audit may run existing checks or allowed temporary diagnostics, but must not edit tracked code, implement new reproducers, or operate a live user cluster; unexecuted scenarios are reproduction plans, not claimed test evidence.

Use an API-server-backed fixture to reconcile an admitted CR twice, inject a conflict or response loss after a successful write, and reconcile with a fresh controller instance; verify external effect count, UID/owner identity and eventual persisted status.

Exercise delete/recreate with the same name and a new UID, delayed child events, terminating owners and failed finalizer cleanup; verify that only the intended resources and external ledger effects are removed.

For scheduled and manual backup runs, interrupt after run creation, Job creation, backup commit, Job completion, result capture and parent summary update; restart the operator and verify run/Job identity, manifest result and Kubernetes-only history retention.

For a successful owned backup Job, inject one Pod-list failure, temporarily absent Pod, log-open failure or interrupted log read, then recover through a fresh reconciler. Verify Running without completion during acquisition, preserved sibling exclusion and Job identity, final literal summary fields and attempt counts, then parent full-summary/incremental eligibility and zero-retention pruning only after terminal accounting. Distinguish malformed acquired payloads and failed Jobs as terminal outcomes; include failed diagnostic writes and repeated unchanged errors.

In an isolated existing restore fixture, preserve PVCs across operator and Ledger process replacement around download/finalize/normal-mode handoffs; verify restored sentinel data and cluster identity independently of management readiness, using a non-empty post-checkpoint delta when incremental restore is exercised.

Exercise scale-down with a real fail-then-success sequence: commit removal then lose exec response, fail the postcondition read once, restart between membership removal and replica update, and retry after cleanup failure. Assert membership, replica count, PVC identity and retained data; also reverse the desired scale while work is incomplete.

Interrupt TLS off/optional/required rollouts in both directions, rotate referenced certs/CA/tokens, and restart the operator with mixed pod revisions; verify authenticated peer/CLI connectivity and final phase from actual pod state. Exercise omitted spec.tls and disabled TLS with an empty secretName. Fail recovery-status persistence before workload changes; interrupt after that persistence and after StatefulSet orphan deletion; resume with a fresh reconciler. Assert optional certificate/CA continuity, unchanged desired spec, recreated mode, retained external Secret, delayed rollout-state cleanup and identical non-empty ledger transaction data after disable. Fake clients prove resource write ordering only; API-server adoption and real peer availability require the corresponding integration fixture.

For Pyroscope authTokenFrom/basicAuthPasswordFrom, distinguish reference edits (Pod-template rollout) from in-place Secret content rotation (explicit Pod restart required). Missing referenced Secrets/keys must remain required container-start dependencies; the operator neither reads nor owns these external credentials. Disclosure of credential bytes belongs to sensitive-data-exposure-boundaries (EN-2061).

Request WAL/data growth using an explicitly expansion-capable disposable storage fixture, interrupt orphan/recreate/adoption and claim updates, and compare template size, each PVC request/capacity, mounted capacity and a persisted sentinel. Exercise unsupported expansion and deletion-protection/retention configurations separately.

Exercise explicit WAL/data size floors with autoExpansion absent and disabled, a mixed group already above the floor, a lower configured floor, and a configured floor above the automatic maximum/cooldown. Start with template 100Gi, live claim 200Gi and configured floor 150Gi; assert template 150Gi, retained claim UID/binding and 200Gi request/capacity, idempotent repeated reconciliation and correct future-claim size. Separately trigger automatic growth and prove it never rewrites the CR or templates. Keep unsupported storageClass/accessMode changes and unchanged hostPath layout in the matrix.

For each size/profile recovery step, fail before and after its durable write, simulate successful writes with lost responses, then use a fresh reconciler. Cover failed snapshot persistence (no orphan delete), retained snapshot after deletion, failed replacement creation, delayed observed generation/adoption and failed snapshot cleanup. Edit desired replicas/image/TLS and make the current CR invalid during recovery; assert the snapshot resumes first, preserves the prior complete Pod template/replicas/selector, freezes later workload changes and is removed only after exact replacement identity/spec, observed generation, all expected nonterminating Pods adopted and retained storage identities verified, without requiring Ready/Updated replicas. Include a changed original source before deletion (safe stale-plan discard and replan), foreign/corrupt snapshot, same-name replacement and ownership guards. Assert Pod/PVC UIDs, PV binding and sentinel data on each intended volume, not only another healthy replica.

Use synthetic inert journals and production preparation paths to assert protected Preparing status precedes CMCreate, preserves sourceUID/full digest/name through generated CRDs, and binds UID only after direct immutable owner/digest verification and decoded source/workload/claim structural validation. Assert a direct journal reread and full reauthentication against the bound UID after binding, before dependencies/deletion/creation; disappearance or changed identity stops the pass. Reject missing fields, changed bytes/full digest/UID/owner, mutable/terminating journals and stale whole-pointer CAS before any dependency or workload mutation. Nil status must neither adopt nor block on standalone journals. Exercise exact AlreadyExists reuse after fresh preparation and intent, plus a different plan deriving a distinct name; do not perform RBAC exploitation or operate a user cluster.

Interrupt after Preparing persistence with no journal; with a fresh reconciler directly observe the same controlled nonterminating source UID, then assert expected CAS clear, handled/two-second requeue and zero dependencies/old-claim reads/normal writes/journal deletion, including unready/changed-generation source and invalid current CR. Reject absent/deleting/replaced/foreign source and uncertain API reads. Deterministically race bind against abort and preserve the winner, then deliver a late journal and prove it remains unbound until fresh full preparation and matching intent. Corrupt a Completed payload and remove immutability; assert owner/UID/RV-fenced cleanup still succeeds, a foreign UID fails and lost-delete-response retry clears only the expected pointer.

Use an explicitly volume-modification-capable CSI fixture to change each WAL/data nonempty profile and distinguish accepted PVC spec from currentVolumeAttributesClassName/modifyVolumeStatus, driver errors and effective profile. Exercise unsupported clearing, missing or mismatched classes, API rejection and real fail-then-success recovery while retaining PVC identity. Assert WALStorageReady/DataStorageReady pending/failure/success separately from ClaimTemplatesReady and automatic-expansion conditions, including status-write conflicts between reconcilers. A fake client proves write ordering only; envtest needs live workload controllers for adoption, and neither proves actual CSI or mounted-filesystem behavior.

With an API-server-backed StatefulSet, combine an adjacent RC update with hostPath-to-PVC and PVC-to-hostPath edits. Assert that the first accepted template changes the image but retains the old Pod storage wiring and claim templates; interrupt and resume with a fresh reconciler, then verify recreation occurs only after all replicas converge. Separately reject skipped RCs and unknown sources after interrupted recreation.

Inject transient API, pod-exec and dependency failures before and after durable effects, restore availability, then assert eventual convergence without unrelated user edits; use deterministic barriers or Eventually assertions rather than sleeps. If envtest, CSI, cert-manager or a separate operator process is unavailable, record that limit explicitly.

At ensureBackupJob, omit desired TLS while an owned optional/required StatefulSet retains certificate and CA references; assert Job transport and mounts. Remove the workload, assert retry with zero Jobs, restore it and create a fresh reconciler, then assert exactly one correctly owned Job. Reject same-name unowned/foreign-owned workloads. Keep previous reservation, lost-response, cache-lag and credential-containment regression triggers with realistic owned StatefulSet fixtures. Independently invoke the Ledger and Cluster in-pod ledgerctl exec boundaries with an absent workload and assert a retryable lookup error before exec; recreate optional, required and disabled workloads and verify mode lookup recovers.

Through the normal envtest manager, create an API-defaulted StatefulSet with the standard probes, supply a settled owned source and retained bound PVC/PVs, then request size/profile alignment. Assert the journal is created and UID-fenced orphan deletion is requested without storage-only Pod-template changes; direct startClaimTemplateRecovery calls do not cover this guard. Reject/timeout normalization once and assert AdmissionCheckFailed and no deletion, then restore admission and prove retry progress. Envtest has no StatefulSet controller or GC; disclose simulated status/ownership and do not claim actual adoption from this fixture.

After deletion, supply the exact owned replacement with observed generation and all expected nonterminating Pods adopted, but ReadyReplicas=0 and UpdatedReplicas=0. Cover unready/OOM and empty-key startup failure states. With a fresh reconciler, persist completion, delete the journal and clear its pointer, then execute a subsequent normal image/configuration/auth-template repair and verify its actual template bytes plus retained storage identities. Separately leave generation unobserved and one Pod missing, terminating or unadopted; each must retain recovery. Keep original pre-delete readiness/cancellation tests. Fake/envtest status and owner updates do not prove real controller adoption, Pod availability, running authorization or GC; those require a live-controller fixture.

Fail the initial recovery resume at source orphan-delete and replacement Create, then succeed with a fresh reconciler. Assert RecoveryFailed survives the preparation defer, the durable-write typed cause is preserved, the retry delay records one failure, the exact bound journal/pointer remains, and storage identities are unchanged. Separately keep pre-handoff PreparationFailed coverage. For automatic PVC optimistic locking, interpose a larger request between the authoritative read and the actual patch; assert a real conflict, retry reread and final larger request/UID/annotations, with no annotations from the rejected patch. Preserve the pre-read larger-request case and mutation-check removal of the lock. Also fail the initial uncached Cluster refresh after journal creation but before authentication/binding. Assert RecoveryFailed, exact retained Preparing pointer/journal, no dependency or workload mutations, single retry accounting and a fresh successful resume that binds and progresses. Through full Reconcile, separately fail an ordinary initial Cluster probe with nil recovery pointer, covering both absent and existing ClaimTemplatesReady. Verify the error propagates without creating or relabeling that persisted condition, then recover the read and stop at invalid-spec validation with no fabricated recovery failure. Retain the known Preparing-pointer positive failure case.

Scale down with retained PVCs, edit a nonempty VolumeAttributesClass and scale up again. Assert current claim templates, unchanged inactive requests while outside live replicas, readiness scoped to active ordinals, ownership validation on reused claims, stable PVC/PV identities and pending-to-ready CSI observation. Inventory all namespaces and requested/current/pending class references plus templates and desired manifests before GitOps class retirement; readiness alone cannot certify no references. Real EKS/EBS acceptance must record Kubernetes/CSI/operator versions, throughput increase/decrease, operator restart, actual adoption, unchanged EBS identities and retained Ledger data.

Through Cluster reconcileStatefulSetWithExec, scale 3 to 1 under omitted Retain, explicit Retain and WhenDeleted=Delete/WhenScaled=Retain. Assert no PVC deletion timestamp and unchanged PVC/PV UIDs, claim binding and volume source, even with PV reclaim Delete. Preserve explicit WhenScaled=Delete membership/removal retry regressions. For the separate hostPath/PVC layout path, reject foreign cached/live owners, stale UIDs/resourceVersions and terminating sources before DELETE. Race replacement and ownership/metadata updates after the direct read against a real API server; assert UID/resourceVersion preconditions cause conflict with the current object intact, and a fresh benign-metadata retry succeeds. Distinguish object preservation from mounted-data proof, which requires live Kubernetes/CSI acceptance.
